audio_caption: The audio clip starts with one female speaker cheerfully introducing a video about how to take notes on an iPad Pro. She begins by listing the hardware she uses, a 2017 10.5 inch iPad Pro, mentioning she ordered it from Amazon renewed for $350. The speaker explains it was a risk, but Amazon had a 90-day return policy. She continues to describe the iPad case, purchased for around $12, followed by the Apple Pencil. During the description, upbeat, playful pop music plays in the background, which seems to fade down slightly when the speaker begins listing the items she uses for note-taking.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker enthusiastically describing an Apple Pencil as "truly amazing", noting its durability and writing quality, and emphasizing the comfort of holding it. She also highlights the game-changing effect of a paper-like screen protector that enhances the writing experience. She indicates that she ordered all the mentioned products from Amazon and will share the links. The clip concludes with her posing the question "So why digital note taking?"

The clip starts with a single female speaker discussing her note-taking experiences during university. She mentions initially being strict with color-coded handwritten notes, transitioning to recording lectures due to time constraints, and ultimately relaxing her method for efficiency. She emphasizes the time-consuming nature of handwritten notes, the physical clutter they create, and how she became emotionally attached to her notes. She concludes that digital note-taking combines the speed of typing with the improved learning from writing by hand. Finally, she mentions the app she uses.

A female speaker begins by stating a price and explaining the value of an app called GoodNotes, citing convenience, simplicity, and organization as key benefits. She elaborates on how she organizes folders and documents within the app, using her biochemistry class as an example, highlighting how she has materials separated for each exam. She then mentions how easy it is to upload documents and PowerPoint presentations onto the app, allowing her to keep all class information in one place, avoiding paper printouts unless she needs to type using Google Docs.

The clip begins with a female speaker describing her preference for a standard notebook with a brown cover and black binding for notes on GoodNotes. She explains that she uses A5-sized gridded paper because writing on grids looks neat and helps her write straight. She also notes that the A5 size is small enough, so the page does not feel overloaded with information and that she finds it comfortable to write on. She adds that she doesn't use the zoom-in feature of the app because she doesn't always reach the end of the line, and the smaller page is a useful alternative.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker describing the pen options in the GoodNotes app and expressing her preference for the ball pen, discussing its size and how she adapts it for different files. She then transitions to discussing her color choices, usually sticking to three colors for notes and changing them when bored. She also highlights text with blue, red, and purple highlighters, mentioning that she uses them to mark important information. The speaker concludes by stating she will preface how she takes notes.

A female speaker discusses her note-taking methods, which vary from class to class. She describes different strategies, such as writing on PowerPoints, using a lecture-style notebook, or sometimes not taking notes at all if the material is already familiar or if the professor just reads from slides. She explains that she now focuses on active revision over extensive note-taking, emphasizing the importance of understandable and useful notes. She then announces a note-taking process.

The clip opens with a female speaker explaining her note-taking process, saying it's "really simple and it works for me." Her tone is casual and conversational. She mentions writing the date in the upper right corner for revision, and then the topic title at the top, which she highlights or circles.

The audio clip consists of one person, a female, speaking in a calm and informative tone. She describes her bullet point system for note taking, using a bullet point for general information, a dash for specific information, and an arrow for even more specific information, repeating this cycle as needed, indicating that this system is helpful for her to keep notes clean and remember significations.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker explaining her approach to taking notes on PowerPoints or pre-made notes. She describes highlighting statements her professor emphasizes, using a different color to add diagrams and information, and adding an asterisk to create practice questions. The speaker maintains a clear and articulate speaking tone throughout. At the end of her description, she trails off stating she can attempt to answer it herself.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker describing her old note-taking system, explaining, "these are notes I took from a biology textbook...and this was basically useless," detailing the issues with condensing information. She contrasts this with using mnemonics or flashcards for better study, and eventually switching to Anki flashcards. Her tone is reflective and slightly critical. During the speech, there's quiet music in the background. She mentions that her new system is more practical. The audio clip ends with her saying, "So yeah, that's it for my note-taking system. Bye."

The audio begins with a female speaker expressing a hope that her content was helpful, mentioning that it's easy to fixate on aesthetics over functionality in studying, and that it's more important to focus on understanding information. She wraps up the video and says goodbye. A bright, upbeat pop music track starts, creating a light and cheerful mood.
